board.description: The board to page through. Omitted, both are served, each sliced by the same `offset` and `limit`; named, the other one comes back empty.

offset.description: Rows to skip on each board, after searching and ordering (default 0). The whole board is reachable, not only its first rows.

sort.description: The column the boards are ordered on (default `fame-points`, the board's own order). `gain` and `move` are the last 24 hours.

order.description: Direction of `sort` (default `desc`). Rows with no figure on the sorted column come last either way.

range.description: The column `min` and `max` bound. A row with no figure on it (a 24h move before the captures reach back a day) is left out.

min.description: Lowest value kept on the `range` column, inclusive.

max.description: Highest value kept on the `range` column, inclusive.

q.description: Case-insensitive search: a player's nickname, or a clan's tag or name. Rows keep their real place.

edition.description: The edition to read, by its identifier (an `eventName` from `editions`). Defaults to the newest edition recorded.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.

metric.description: Rating metric the leaderboard is ranked by. `pr` (Personal Rating) and `wtr` (World of Tanks Rating) are Wargaming's account figures and exist on lifetime boards only: a recent period or a per-vehicle board asked for either answers with its `wnx` ranking.

edition.description: The edition to read, by its identifier. Defaults to the newest edition recorded.

period.description: Window the stats are computed over: the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or all-time (default overall).

mode.description: Which battle mode to count, random by default. Modes are never pooled: each has its own team size, length and idea of a good result, so every figure in the response belongs to the one asked for. The modes field says which ones hold battles on this map.

player.description: The account whose battle the card shows: their result, vehicle and figures. Without it, the battle as a whole.

id.description: The game's own battle id (`arenaUniqueID`), as digits. A string, not a number: it runs to 19 digits.

slugs.description: Columns to compare (2 to 4). A slug on its own, or suffixed with the game client to read it on (`is-7@ct`) or with its position among the columns showing that same vehicle (`is-7~2`, one tank under two setups).

page.description: Which page of `limit` battles, counted from one. The first by default; `total` in the answer says how many there are.

limit.description: Battles per page, 20 by default, 100 at most.

sort.description: What the replays are ranked by: the damage their recorder dealt (`damage`, the default), their assisted damage, experience or kills, the newest first (`recent`), or the most opened (`views`) or downloaded (`downloads`).

mode.description: Only battles of this mode, by the game's own `bonusType` (1 is random battles). `facets.modes` lists the ones the catalogue has.

tank.description: Only replays recorded in this vehicle, by its tank id. `facets.tanks` lists the ones the catalogue has.

map.description: Only battles on this arena, by the game's own map id (`05_prohorovka`). `facets.maps` lists the ones the catalogue has.

result.description: Only replays whose recorder won, lost or drew.

version.description: Only battles of this game update, as `2.4.1` (any hotfix of it), or `latest` for the newest update the catalogue holds. `versions` lists the ones it has.

facets.description: `true` to also answer what each filter can take, counted.

id.description: The game's own battle id (`arenaUniqueID`), as digits. A string, not a number: it runs to 19 digits.

window.description: How far back an account counts as active.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.

sort.description: Ranking column: `total` for three-mark guns across every tier, or `tier-<n>` for one tier (`tier-10`). Default `total`, which is also what an unrecognised value falls back to. Not an enum: which tiers the game has is Wargaming's to decide, and the response's `tiers` names the ones this region has a ranking for.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.

offset.description: Rows to skip before the page begins, applied to the standings AND to the lost places, so one pair of parameters pages both. The aggregates always describe the whole board, whatever the slice.

season.description: Season event id to load (default the current season). From the seasons list in the response.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.
Maximum number of rows to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.

metric.description: Rating metric the leaderboard is ranked by. `pr` (Personal Rating) and `wtr` (World of Tanks Rating) are Wargaming's account figures and exist on lifetime boards only: a recent period or a per-vehicle board asked for either answers with its `wnx` ranking.

tools.description: Win rate by tier and rating band

id.description: The game's own battle id (`arenaUniqueID`), as digits. A string, not a number: it runs to 19 digits.

recorder.description: The account whose recording to read, one of the battle's `recorders`. Each participant who recorded the battle has their own point of view; without it, the battle's first recording.

id.description: The game's own battle id (`arenaUniqueID`), as digits. A string, not a number: it runs to 19 digits.

page.description: Which page of `limit` battles, newest first, counted from one. The first by default; `total` in the answer says how many there are.

mode.description: Only battles of this mode, by the game's own `bonusType` (1 is random battles). `facets.modes` lists the ones this account has.

tank.description: Only battles this account fought in this vehicle, by its tank id. `facets.tanks` lists the ones it has.

map.description: Only battles on this arena, by the game's own map id (`05_prohorovka`). `facets.maps` lists the ones it has.

result.description: Only battles this account won, lost or drew.

facets.description: `true` to also answer `facets`: every mode, vehicle, map and result this account's battles have, counted over all of them regardless of the filters above. Left out by default, since only a page that draws filters needs it.

limit.description: Battles per page, newest first. Ten by default, a hundred at most.

season.description: Season event id to load (default the current season). From the seasons list on the leaderboard.

mode.description: Only count battles of this mode, by the game's own `bonusType` (1 is random battles).

tank.description: Only count battles this account fought in this vehicle, by its tank id.

map.description: Only count battles on this arena, by the game's own map id (`05_prohorovka`).

result.description: Only count battles this account won, lost or drew.

range.description: How far back the population series reads.

tools.description: Credits and experience by battle mode

range.description: How far back the population series reads.

names.description: Player nicknames, case-insensitive. Up to 100. The nickname an account wears NOW, never one it used to: a roster shows who is in the room, and answering through a name history would confidently name an account that no longer answers to what the roster printed.

vehicles.description: `<account id>:<vehicle id>` pairs, up to 60. Each one is answered in `vehicles` with what that account has done on that vehicle. The vehicle id is Wargaming's `tank_id`, which is the game client's own compact descriptor, so a client reads it off the roster it is drawing.

mode.description: Which mode the `vehicles` figures should cover. Omitted, they cover every mode together. Frontline, Onslaught and Steel Hunter are absent on purpose: Wargaming publishes no per-vehicle statistics for them at all, so a client in one of those battles omits this and reads the whole record.

videoId.description: Narrow to one video's battles, ordered by timestamp.

slugs.description: Columns to compare (2 to 4). A slug on its own, or suffixed with the game client to read it on (`is-7@ct`) or with its position among the columns showing that same vehicle (`is-7~2`, one tank under two setups).

token.description: Signed moderator link, from the moderation channel.

client.description: Which game client to read the vehicle's characteristics from. `ct` serves what the running Common Test build makes of it, so a tank can be inspected and configured the way the next update would ship it. Falls back to live when no test is running or when it leaves this vehicle alone.

mode.description: Which battle mode to count, random by default. Modes are never pooled: each has its own economy and its own idea of a good result, so every figure in the response belongs to the one asked for. The modes field says which ones hold anything for this vehicle.

twins.description: Count this vehicle's twins with it, false by default: the vehicles that are this one under another name, listed in the tank detail's `twins` (the Dream Chaser is the SDP wz 66 Grom). Wargaming records each id apart, so their battles are otherwise counted on their own page only. Each best player's `tankId` says which of them their row is on.

limit.description: How many matches to return. Out-of-range values are clamped.

status.description: Only tournaments in this lifecycle state.
